text:
Ben Kindel has 7 points in 14 games for a Penguins team that has lost most of his last ten, and he has missed time this season. When he came back on Oct. 29 he had two points against Utah before Logan Cooley's overtime winner spoiled the night. The numbers since are thin: 3 points in ten games.

Don't read too much into that. Pittsburgh has scored 9.0 fewer goals than its chances deserve with Kindel on the ice, one of the biggest gaps in the league. His own finishing (3 goals on 3.53 expected) is fine. It's the team around him that isn't converting. At 5v5, Pittsburgh is losing his minutes, which is normal for a 19-year-old center taken 11th last summer.

Forwards drafted where he went score a median 0.37 points a game in their first real season; he is at 0.50. He carries the puck in on 56 percent of his entries, per a small sample of Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. Expect the points to pick up as the luck evens out.
headline: Kindel's rookie line is better than it looks
